note: #3067 (research 0028 row A15; seat:caa's rulings on #3067, Q1 to Q3): the ONE classification of a sealed clause, HAND-AUTHORED from the checker's gates, which every core replays through `check`'s scope gate and through the contract tier's one function. A case is one sealed clause of `program` (`clause` is its index), classified in a context: `seals` (the relations its certificate seals), `reads_lower` (the relations it reads from a strictly lower certificate) and `owns` (the relations a theory owns, decided live). The dependency graph is built over `program` with `seals` as its scope, as check builds it. `expect` is null when the clause is inside the certifiable fragment, else the FIRST gate it fails and that gate's subject. The gates, in their one order (seat:caa's Q1, the checker's order): (1) the count gate, per count literal in body order, `count_not_lower` then `count_open_compound`; (2) `constructor_cycle`; (3) the read gate, per body literal in body order, `unserved` then `intra_scope_negation`; (4) range restriction, `unbound_count_filter` per count literal in body order, then `unbound_variable`. Where a gate names a variable it names the first unbound one in name order. Notation: a string starting with an upper-case letter is a variable, any other string an atom, an array a compound `[functor, args...]`; a body literal is a goal, `{"neg": goal}` or `{"count": {pred, arity, filter: [[position, term]...], result}}` (a `count` over rows).

cases.name: a_count_over_this_scope_is_not_lower
cases.note: The counted q is sealed by the clause's own certificate: a count must read a strictly lower one, never the table under construction.

cases.name: a_count_over_a_relation_nothing_seals_is_not_lower
cases.note: No certificate seals the counted q.

cases.name: a_count_filter_carrying_an_open_compound
cases.note: q is read lower, but the filter term f(Y) is an open compound, which the count gate refuses.

cases.name: a_constructor_on_its_own_cycle
cases.note: nat(s(X)) :- nat(X) constructs s(X) on nat's own dependency cycle. The fact nat(z) is in scope and inside the fragment.

cases.name: a_read_nothing_serves
cases.note: q is neither sealed, nor theory-owned, nor read from a lower certificate.

cases.name: a_negation_of_a_relation_this_scope_seals
cases.note: q is sealed by the clause's own certificate, so \+ q would read the table under construction.

cases.name: a_count_filter_variable_nothing_binds
cases.note: The filter binds position 0 of q to Y, and no positive sealed literal binds Y.

cases.name: a_variable_nothing_binds
cases.note: X occurs only under \+, and a negated literal binds nothing.

cases.name: a_theory_literal_binds_nothing
cases.note: eq is theory-owned, so it is served, but a theory literal binds no variable: X is bound by nothing.

cases.name: inside_the_fragment
cases.note: The control: r is sealed and binds X, and q is read lower under \+.

cases.name: a_lower_read_binds
cases.note: The control for reads_lower: q is read from a strictly lower certificate, and a positive lower read binds X.

cases.name: the_count_gate_before_the_cycle_gate
cases.note: Adjacent pair (count, cycle): the filter f(M) is an open compound AND the head constructs s(N) on nat's cycle. The count gate wins.

cases.name: the_cycle_gate_before_the_read_gate
cases.note: Adjacent pair (cycle, read): nat(s(X)) constructs on nat's cycle AND reads zz, which nothing serves. The cycle gate wins.

cases.name: the_read_gate_before_range_restriction
cases.note: Adjacent pair (read, range): \+ q negates a relation this scope seals AND X is bound by nothing. The read gate wins.

cases.name: the_cycle_gate_before_range_restriction_3067
cases.note: #3067's witness: p(f(X)) :- p(Y) is unsafe (X is bound by nothing) AND constructs on p's cycle. check named the cycle; every seal plan named 'is not range-restricted'. The one order names the cycle.

cases.name: within_the_count_gate_not_lower_before_open_compound
cases.note: One count literal fails both count checks: q is sealed by this scope AND its filter f(Y) is an open compound. Not-lower comes first.

cases.name: within_the_read_gate_body_order_decides
cases.note: The read gate runs literal by literal: zz (unserved) is read before \+ s (intra-scope), so unserved is named.

cases.name: within_the_read_gate_body_order_decides_reversed
cases.note: The same two literals in the other order: \+ s comes first, so intra-scope negation is named.

cases.name: within_range_restriction_a_filter_before_a_variable
cases.note: The filter variable Y and the head variable Z are both unbound. The count filter is named first.

cases.name: the_first_unbound_variable_in_name_order
cases.note: Y (in the head) and X (under \+) are both unbound. The one order names X, the first in name order, wherever it occurs. Before #3067, ts named Y (occurrence order) and go named either (a map's iteration order).

cases.name: the_first_unbound_count_filter_variable_in_name_order
cases.note: The filter binds q's position 0 to Y and position 1 to X, both unbound. The one order names X, the first in name order. Before #3067, rs and ts named Y (occurrence order).

cases.name: a_lower_read_a_theory_owns_binds_nothing_3067
cases.note: seat:caa's ruling on #3067 increment 2, Q1: near, read lower, binds X only if no theory owns it. check's partition gate refuses a certificate that seals a theory's relation, so for check a relation read lower is never owned and this changes nothing. The resolver reads the standard theory while its plan seals every relation but the arithmetic builtins, so it can put a theory's relation (=) in a lower layer, and there too it binds nothing, so X is bound by nothing that must bind.
